problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-t{y}^{′}+10y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=t({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-t{y}^{′}+10y=0,\,y(1)=2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=-4,\,t>0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Cauchy-Euler Equations: Characteristic Equations With Complex Roots

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-2t{y}^{′}+20y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=t({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-2t{y}^{′}+20y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=-2,\,t>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=-2,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =({c}_{1}+3{c}_{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+({c}_{2}-3{c}_{1})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=-2$ and ${c}_{1}=1$ into the above to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =1+3{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(t)=t(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).
$$
